name: MAC & HMAC Assessment
description: Assessment of message authentication code (MAC) implementations including HMAC, CMAC, GMAC, and Poly1305. Covers key management for MAC keys, constant-time comparison verification, truncation risks, and correct usage patterns for integrity and authentication.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to MAC or HMAC assessment

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands MAC concepts and the difference between MACs and plain hashes
evidence: Can explain why a MAC requires a secret key and a plain hash does not
Understands the HMAC construction and its purpose
Can describe when MACs are used versus digital signatures

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Identifies MAC usage and basic implementation issues under supervision
evidence: Identifies HMAC usage in APIs, authentication tokens, and protocol implementations
Detects use of plain hashes where MACs are required under guidance
Reviews code for MAC key management practices
Documents MAC-related findings following lab templates

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses MAC implementations for correctness and security
evidence: Identifies timing-based MAC verification vulnerabilities (non-constant-time comparison)
Evaluates HMAC key derivation and rotation practices
Assesses MAC tag truncation and its impact on forgery resistance
Produces findings referencing RFC 2104, FIPS 198-1, NIST SP 800-38B (CMAC), or relevant standards

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Handles complex MAC assessment scenarios; demonstrates timing attacks in lab
evidence: Demonstrates timing-based MAC forgery attacks in lab environments
Evaluates CMAC and GMAC implementations in protocol contexts
Assesses MAC usage in key derivation (HKDF) and key wrapping constructions
Reviews and mentors junior staff on MAC assessment methodology

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines MAC assessment methodology; recognised authority on MAC security
evidence: Authored or maintains the lab's MAC assessment methodology
Published research on MAC implementation vulnerabilities or timing attacks
Provides expert guidance on MAC scheme selection and integration patterns
Trains teams on MAC internals, failure modes, and assessment approaches

assessment_methods.description: Assess an API using HMAC-based authentication: evaluate key management, comparison logic, and tag handling
Given an application with a timing side-channel in MAC verification, demonstrate exploitation and propose a fix
